# A `Transaction` naming one `PaymentSplit`, stating an amount that is not it.
#
# `amount: 999` beside a split carrying 60.00. The sum check is written for a
# block naming several, so a block naming one fell past it — and its slot
# carries the guid, so the pairing matches by that and `_single_payment_matches`
# never reads `amount:` either.
#
# The key spelling is *not* the comparison here, and an earlier version of this
# note said it was. `amount:` means a different figure there —
# `_bank_side_figure_of` reads it as what moved through the bank, residue
# included — so the two are weighed differently on purpose, and README says
# which is which.
#
# What that costs is the same "one file, two meanings" the sum check exists
# for: in the book holding the transaction the split settles 60.00, and in one
# that does not the guids resolve to nothing and 999.00 is entered from the
# block.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal quoting the 999.00 stated and the 60.00
# named.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-27
    amount: 999
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    Transaction "5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445"
      PaymentSplit "708192a3b4c5d6e7f809122334455667"
